subject: Finera: request for key-lifecycle & transport cipher evidence
messages:
From: Alex Bolton <alex.bolton@finera.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finera.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finera: request for key-lifecycle & transport cipher evidence

Michael —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. As part of our SOC 2 and SIG intake we need a compact set of artifacts that demonstrate Redwood's key management controls. At minimum Finera's security team has asked for:

- A short runbook describing the key rotation procedure (who initiates, approval gates, automation steps, rollback).
- Example rotation event (audit log extract) showing a real rotation with timestamps and operator identity.
- HSM attestation or vendor proof that keys are protected in FIPS 140-2/3 or equivalent HSMs.
- Details on envelope encryption: KEK wrapping algorithm, supported key lengths, and whether customer BYOK is supported.
- TLS/in-transit cipher policy (min TLS version, allowed cipher suites) and any TLS termination points.

Can you tell me what you can provide by end of day Wednesday? We prefer redacted logs rather than full operational data. If you have a single bundle or drive link that contains the items above that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Bolton
Security Engineer, Finera
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Bolton <alex.bolton@finera.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finera: request for key-lifecycle & transport cipher evidence

Alex —

Thanks, this is clear. We can assemble a compact evidence bundle with the items you listed. High level notes below and then a proposed deliverable list.

Short answers:
- Runbook: we have a concise operational runbook covering automated rotation, manual override, canary rollout and rollback steps. Will provide as PDF.
- Rotation event: we'll provide a redacted CSV extract (timestamps, rotation-id, operator-id, key-id, pre/post status).
- HSM attestation: we can include our vendor attestation PDF and a reference to the HSM serials used in the cluster (redacted).
- Envelope encryption: we use AES-256-GCM for data keys wrapped with RSA-OAEP-256 or ECDH-ES with X25519 for compatible BYOK flows; I will include algorithms and config snippets.
- TLS policy: minimum TLS 1.2 for legacy customers, TLS 1.3 recommended; termination occurs at the load balancer in hosted deployments, for private deployments termination is customer-managed. Cipher list will be attached.

Proposed deliverables (attached or links):
1) kms_runbook_v1.pdf — short runbook and diagram.
2) rotation-audit-snapshot.csv — redacted sample of a rotation event.
3) hsm-attestation-reference.pdf — vendor attestation (redacted serials).
4) Drive folder with configuration snippets and cipher lists (link below).

Before I package: two quick clarifications so we deliver exactly what you need —
- Do you need operator identities mapped to full employee names for your audit, or will hashed/operator-id values suffice?
- Do you want a live SIG/CAIQ sheet filled out, or do you only need the raw evidence artifacts?

I can get the bundle to you by EOD Wednesday (2028-07-04) if you confirm the above.

— Michael Grant
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Link (working folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4Finera-KMS-Evidence
From: Alex Bolton <alex.bolton@finera.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finera.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finera: request for key-lifecycle & transport cipher evidence

Thanks Michael — that lineup looks good. A couple of clarifications:

- Operator identities: hashed/operator-id values are fine for now; we may request mapping during the later compliance window but this initial artifact set is OK redacted.
- SIG/CAIQ: please provide the raw artifacts first; we'll request a completed SIG spreadsheet if needed.

A few follow-ups from the Finera crypto team:
1) Can you include your HSM vendor name and whether the HSM is single-tenant or multi-tenant per cluster?
2) Provide the retention policy for KMS audit events and whether export to S3/secure archive is supported for customer review.
3) Do you support hardware-backed BYOK where the customer supplies the wrapping key (customer-managed KEK)? If so, any limits on key algorithms?

If you can include short answers inline with the bundle it will speed our review. ETA Wednesday EOD works.

— Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Bolton <alex.bolton@finera.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finera: request for key-lifecycle & transport cipher evidence

Alex —

Attached is a compact evidence bundle that addresses Finera's list plus the follow-ups you requested. Summary below and attachments included.

What we attached:
- kms_runbook_v1.pdf (short runbook + sequence diagram)
- rotation-audit-snapshot.csv (redacted sample rotation event; contains rotation-id, operator-id hash, key-id prefix, UTC timestamps)
- hsm-attestation-reference.pdf (vendor attestation; redacted serials)
- cipher-policy.txt (allowed TLS ciphers and default priority)
- byok-supported-modes.txt (BYOK modes and algorithm constraints)

Short inline answers:
- HSM vendor & tenancy: We use a FIPS-validated HSM provider (vendor name included in hsm-attestation-reference.pdf). HSMs in the hosted control plane are single-tenant per customer cluster for Dedicated/Private deployments; in shared-hosted tiers we use logical separation with hardware-backed keys (details in attestation).
- Audit retention & export: KMS audit events are retained for 365 days by default; export to customer-owned S3 with SSE-KMS or to an encrypted archive is supported for Dedicated/Private customers (we included a sample retention/config snippet in the Drive link).
- BYOK: We support hardware-backed BYOK (customer-provided KEK) for Private and Dedicated deployments. Supported wrapping algorithms: RSA-OAEP-256 and ECDH-ES (X25519) for release parity. See byok-supported-modes.txt for limitations and recommended key sizes.

Delivery notes:
- All logs are redacted to remove PII and privileged user emails. If you require mapping for a later audit window we can provide a signed operator mapping under an NDA.
- The Drive folder contains CLI snippets and config templates for enabling BYOK and exporting audit logs.

Drive link (same folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4Finera-KMS-Evidence
HubSpot (deal): https://app.hubspot.com/deal/D-8391

If you want a completed SIG spreadsheet, let me know and we can prioritize that for Thursday.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 180KB); rotation-audit-snapshot.csv (CSV, 12KB); hsm-attestation-reference.pdf (PDF, 95KB); cipher-policy.txt (TXT, 4KB); byok-supported-modes.txt (TXT, 3KB)
